stories.headline: Hantavirus crisis: Lecornu takes charge of government response as French patient remains in intensive care
stories.summary: A French passenger from the MV Hondius cruise ship tested positive for Andes hantavirus and was placed in intensive care at Paris's Bichat hospital. Prime Minister Lecornu led daily interministerial meetings, ordered mandatory hospital quarantine for all contact cases without exception, and called for tighter EU-Schengen protocol coordination; France's Pasteur Institute confirmed the virus matches known South American strains. Health Minister Rist was also highly visible in communications, though final decisions flowed from Matignon.

stories.headline: Macron nominee for Banque de France governorship faces cronyism accusations ahead of parliamentary hearing
stories.summary: Emmanuel Macron's choice of Emmanuel Moulin — his former Élysée secretary-general — to succeed François Villeroy de Galhau as Banque de France governor drew broad accusations of 'recasage' (rewarding allies with top posts), compounded by revelations that the Bank's staff had prepared briefing notes for Moulin ahead of his May 20 parliamentary hearing. Economy Minister Lescure defended the nomination; LFI and RN both announced they would vote against, making parliamentary approval uncertain.

stories.headline: Fuel prices at record high due to Middle East war as Lecornu delays then schedules new aid package for June
stories.summary: Petrol prices in France reached their highest level since the start of the Iran war on 27 February, exceeding €2 per litre for SP95; fiscal revenues from fuel fell sharply as consumption dropped ~30%, undermining a 'windfall' narrative. Prime Minister Lecornu announced he would present a new support package for heavy drivers and affected sectors on Thursday 21 May, after weeks of criticism for slow action.

stories.headline: RN and 2027 presidential campaign: Le Pen's candidacy status, Bardella preparations, electorate expansion
stories.summary: With the July 7 appeal verdict looming, Marine Le Pen confirmed she will run in 2027 if convicted only with a suspended sentence; RN president Bardella meanwhile conducted German outreach (FAZ interview), met employer groups, and launched an economic adviser. A Fondation Jean-Jaurès study found 45% of French voters now consider RN a possible vote, identifying four distinct electoral families. Coverage also addressed Édouard Philippe's attempts to frame a centre-right vs. RN duel.

stories.headline: 2027 left-wing presidential race: primaire collapse as Mélenchon, Ruffin, Glucksmann jockey for position

Mélenchon meanwhile mobilised LFI networks and articulated his 'nouvelle France' electoral strategy.

stories.headline: Macron's Africa Forward summit in Nairobi yields €23bn investment pledge but raises questions on France's retreat
stories.summary: President Macron attended the Africa Forward 2026 summit in Nairobi (11–12 May) co-hosted with Kenyan President Ruto, pledging €23 billion in development commitments and acknowledging France had been 'overtaken' by Turkey, China and the US on the continent. The visit included a stop in Ethiopia to meet PM Abiy Ahmed, and prompted commentary on whether France's 'Françafrique' model can be reformed.

Le JDD described 'a week where everything unravels,' Le Figaro warned of 'a final high-risk year,' and former ministers from his own camp publicly criticised his governance style. stories.headline: French intelligence probes Israeli firm BlackCore for alleged electoral interference against LFI candidates
stories.summary: Reuters reported that French intelligence agencies are investigating whether Israeli firm BlackCore ran a disinformation campaign — including fake websites — targeting three LFI municipal election candidates in Marseille, Toulouse, and Roubaix ahead of March's elections. Mélenchon publicly demanded a law against foreign interference; Israel's Foreign Ministry said it was unaware of BlackCore.
